title: lab.common.coherence.sequence_coherence wired into write_long_document's per-leaf render loop as coherence_flags
goal: Give lab.common.coherence.sequence_coherence -- a confirmed-dormant module whose own follow-ups already named the gap -- its first real wiring into the live long-form writing path, and prove the wiring doesn't bury its own signal under a title-vs-sentence artifact found while building it.
method: Two two-finding fixtures about the same entity (so both findings land in one leaf, making this a within-leaf question, not working_memory's cross-page one): one with a genuine unsignaled topic jump, one with a genuinely related second fact. Both run through write_long_document end to end, checking coherence_flags fires on the first and stays empty on the second, and that the leaf's own title never appears inside a flagged pair on either the default (newline-joined) or plain_english=True (space-joined) rendering path.

jump_coherence_flags.first: Ravi Sharma lives at 14 MG Road, Pune 411001.
jump_coherence_flags.second: Also, Ravi Sharma mentioned that the weather forecast predicts heavy rain in Mumbai next week.

results_prose: A leaf with a genuine within-leaf unsignaled topic jump (Ravi Sharma's address, then an unrelated weather remark) -> 1 coherence flag(s): [{'leaf_id': 'E0000', 'index': 0, 'first': 'Ravi Sharma lives at 14 MG Road, Pune 411001.', 'second': 'Also, Ravi Sharma mentioned that the weather forecast predicts heavy rain in Mumbai next week.', 'similarity': 0.6064, 'opening_connective': None, 'opening_connective_operator': None, 'flagged': True}]. The same shape with a genuinely related second finding instead -> 0 flag(s) (expect 0). The leaf's own title never appears as either side of a flagged pair in either case (title_leaked=False) -- confirms the title-vs-first-sentence bug found while wiring this is actually fixed, not just avoided by luck on one fixture. plain_english=True (a different code path, no newline between title and body) -> 1 flag(s), same result, no crash.
conclusion: lab.common.coherence.sequence_coherence is now wired into lab.common.longform.write_long_document's per-leaf render loop, reported as coherence_flags alongside the existing consistency_flags -- a genuine within-leaf topic jump is caught, a genuinely coherent leaf produces zero false positives, and the leaf's own title (joined to its body by template_rewriter.splice_unit's own newline convention, which lab.common.textutil.sentences treats as a sentence boundary) never leaks into the comparison as a fake 'sentence' on either the newline-joined or the plain_english space-joined path. This closes EXP-050's own named follow-up, generalized one level up (write_long_document's render loop, where rendered sentences actually exist) from where it suggested wiring it (build_outline, before any sentence is rendered).
scale_down: Two two-finding fixtures, one entity -- a proof the wiring works end to end and the title-leak bug is fixed, not a coherence-detection benchmark at document scale (EXP-050's own 103-sentence real-GDPR-text measurement already covers that separately).
follow_ups: coherence_flags is reported but nothing downstream (brain.py's trace, or a caller) surfaces it to a reader yet, same 'report, don't yet act on it' posture contract_violations started with before this -- a next step could decide whether a flagged leaf should be reordered, annotated inline, or just left in the trace for now.

Only checked within a single leaf (two findings, same entity) -- a leaf with 3+ findings where the jump is in the middle of the sequence, or a leaf built from the template_id path instead of entity-grouping, is untested here.
models_used: bge-small-en-v1.5 (lab.common.real_encoders, coherence.py's own similarity leg) -- non-generative; template_rewriter.splice_unit (deterministic) renders every leaf, no generative model anywhere in this path as of the 2026-11-11 rewriter withdrawal.
